subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which three components typically make up an automated system?
options: Sensors, microprocessor and actuators
Keyboard, monitor and printer
Router, switch and modem
Hard disk, RAM and cache
questions.explain: An automated system senses conditions with sensors, processes the data with a microprocessor and responds through actuators.

questions.q: What is the main role of a sensor in an automated system?
options: To collect data about a physical quantity from the surroundings
To carry out a physical movement or action
To store the program instructions permanently
To display processed results to the user
questions.explain: A sensor measures a physical quantity such as temperature or light and sends that data to the microprocessor.

questions.q: Why does an automated system need an actuator?
options: To convert control signals into a physical action such as movement
To convert analogue sensor readings into digital data
To reason about data using stored rules
To reduce the amount of electricity the system uses
questions.explain: An actuator turns the microprocessor's output signal into a physical response, for example opening a valve or turning a motor.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an actuator?
options: A motor
A light sensor
A microprocessor
A pressure sensor
questions.explain: A motor is an actuator because it produces physical movement in response to a control signal.

questions.q: Which of these is an advantage of using an automated system in a factory?
options: It can operate continuously with consistent output
It removes the need for any electricity supply
It guarantees no maintenance is ever required
It has a very low initial installation cost
questions.explain: Automated systems can run 24/7 and produce consistent results without the fatigue that affects human workers.

questions.q: An automatic weather station records rainfall, temperature and wind speed without staff present. What part of the system gathers the temperature reading?
options: A temperature sensor
An actuator
The microprocessor
The data-logging software
questions.explain: The temperature reading is captured by a temperature sensor, which feeds the value to the processor for logging.

questions.q: Which set of characteristics best describes a robot?
options: It has a mechanical structure, electrical components and is programmable
It has no moving parts and cannot be reprogrammed
It runs only on paper-based instructions
It must always look like a human being
questions.explain: A robot combines a physical mechanical framework, electrical/electronic components and programmable control.

questions.q: What does it mean to say a robot is 'programmable'?
options: Its behaviour is controlled by software instructions that can be changed
It can only ever perform one fixed task built into its hardware
It works without any electrical power
It must be operated manually at all times
questions.explain: Being programmable means the robot follows stored software instructions that can be modified to change its behaviour.

questions.q: Why are robots often used for tasks such as bomb disposal or working in nuclear plants?
options: They can operate safely in hazardous environments dangerous to humans
They are always cheaper than employing a human worker
They can think creatively about unexpected problems
They never require any programming
questions.explain: Robots can work in dangerous conditions, removing the risk to human life in hazardous environments.

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using robots in manufacturing?
options: They can lead to human job losses
They produce inconsistent results
They are unable to work continuously
They cannot perform repetitive tasks
questions.explain: Replacing human workers with robots can cause unemployment, which is a common disadvantage of automation.

questions.q: A car factory uses machines to weld and paint car bodies on an assembly line. These machines are best described as:
options: Industrial robots
Expert systems
Sensors
Web servers
questions.explain: Programmable machines that carry out physical tasks such as welding and spraying on a production line are industrial robots.

questions.q: Which statement best defines artificial intelligence (AI)?
options: Machines or systems that simulate intelligent human behaviour
Any device that stores large amounts of data
A network that connects computers together
Software that only performs arithmetic calculations
questions.explain: AI refers to computer systems designed to mimic intelligent human behaviour such as reasoning and learning.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key characteristic of an AI system?
options: The ability to learn and adapt from data
The inability to change its behaviour
A guarantee that it never makes mistakes
A requirement that it uses no data at all
questions.explain: AI systems are characterised by collecting data, reasoning with it, and the ability to learn and adapt.

questions.q: What is meant by 'narrow AI'?
options: AI designed to perform a single specific task
AI that can perform any intellectual task a human can
AI that requires no computer to run
AI that has genuine human emotions
questions.explain: Narrow AI is focused on one specific task, such as facial recognition, rather than general human-level intelligence.

questions.q: How does machine learning differ from a traditional program?
options: The system improves its performance by learning from data rather than following only fixed rules
It runs without any data whatsoever
It can never change its outputs once written
It relies solely on the user entering answers manually
questions.explain: Machine learning enables a system to learn patterns from data and improve over time instead of relying only on fixed programmed rules.

questions.q: Which technology allows a computer to understand and respond to human speech or text?
options: Natural language processing
Actuator control
Optical fibre transmission
Disk defragmentation
questions.explain: Natural language processing (NLP) enables AI systems to interpret and respond to human language.

questions.q: An AI system uses a knowledge base and a set of rules. Which component applies the rules to the stored knowledge to draw conclusions?
options: The inference engine
The actuator
The sensor
The knowledge base
questions.explain: The inference engine applies the rules base to the knowledge base to reason and reach conclusions.

questions.q: An online help service answers customer questions by interpreting typed messages and replying in natural language. This is an example of:
options: An AI chatbot using natural language processing
An automated actuator
A simple pressure sensor
A robotic assembly arm
questions.explain: Interpreting typed language and replying conversationally is an AI chatbot using natural language processing.

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of introducing an automated system?
options: High initial setup and installation costs
It can never work in dangerous environments
It always produces inconsistent results
It cannot operate for long periods
questions.explain: A major drawback of automation is the large initial cost of buying and installing the equipment.

questions.q: A photo app is trained on thousands of images that have each been tagged as 'cat' or 'dog' so it can classify new photos. What kind of data was used to train it?
options: Labelled data
Encrypted data
Compressed data
Corrupted data
questions.explain: Training a machine learning model with examples that already carry the correct tags uses labelled data.
